# PicoCalc Remote Keyboard/Mouse

*README.MD file mostly generated by Anthropic's Claude AI because Thomas Dzubin hates documenting code.  LOL*

Author: Thomas Dzubin    License: MIT    Version: V0.01A (set in [version.h](version.h); shown by the demo, the relay window title and the relay console)

Use your PC's keyboard and mouse with a ClockworkPi PicoCalc over the USB cable.
A small C library (`remote/`) goes into your PicoCalc program and gives it keyboard
and mouse events; a ready-made desktop program (the **relay**, `desktop/`)
captures the PC's keyboard and mouse and sends them over. It works the other way
too: the PicoCalc can print text lines on the PC, and (on Windows) its own keyboard
can type into the PC.

**Want to use it in your own PicoCalc program? Read [INTEGRATION.md](INTEGRATION.md).**
It covers adding mouse control to a program and using the PC keyboard instead of the
PicoCalc's, with copy-and-paste code, the function reference, and the gotchas.

```
  PC keyboard/mouse --> relay (SDL2) --USB serial--> PicoCalc program (uses remote/)
                                     <-- text, your own data, PicoCalc's keys --
```

## What is in this folder

| Folder | What it is |
|--------|-----------|
| **`remote/`** | **The library. This is what you copy into your own project.** `remote_input.c/.h` is the API; the rest is its USB setup, the packet format, a key-code helper, an optional PicoCalc-keyboard reader and a two-line CMake helper |
| **`desktop/`** | The relay program for Windows and Linux. Works with any program that uses the library |
| `examples/` | `remote_test.c`: the smallest useful program, about 80 lines. Start here |
| `demo/` | The cursor demo: an arrow that follows the mouse plus a text area. A proof of concept that the library works. Not needed for your own project |
| `picocalc-text-starter-main/` | Vendored picocalc-text-starter by Blair Leduc (LCD, fonts, south-bridge keyboard). Read-only. The library does not need it; the demo and the optional keyboard reader use it |

### The library, `remote/`

| File | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `remote_input.c/.h` | The API: `remote_input_init()`, `remote_input_task()`, `remote_input_get_event()`, `remote_log()`, `remote_send()` |
| `remote_protocol.h` | The packet format, shared byte for byte with the relay |
| `usb_descriptors.c`, `usb_descriptors_config.h`, `tusb_config.h`, `remote_config.h` | Make the PicoCalc appear as a USB serial port; the library's constants |
| `hid_keymap.c/.h` | USB HID key code to ASCII and back (US layout), names for special keys |
| `picocalc_keys.c/.h`, `picocalc_keys_config.h` | Optional: reads the PicoCalc's own keyboard as key events, plus the `~` = reboot to BOOTSEL shortcut |
| `remote.cmake` | `remote_add_to_target(my_program)`: adds all of the above to your build |

### The relay, `desktop/`

| File | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `relay.c` | The relay itself: window, capture, sending, receiving. Portable C. Start with the reading guide at the top of the file |
| `relay_serial.c/.h` | The serial port, and finding the PicoCalc by USB ID (Windows and Linux) |
| `relay_inject.c/.h`, `relay_inject_keys.h` | Typing the PicoCalc's keys into the PC: Windows (`SendInput`); a stub on Linux for now |
| `relay_mirror.c/.h` | Optional, demo support: draws the cursor demo's screen in the relay window. Off with `-DRELAY_WITH_MIRROR=OFF` |
| `relay_config.h` | Window, colours and other constants |
| `pico/stdlib.h` | A stand-in for the Pico SDK header, so the relay can use the starter's font |

## Building

### PicoCalc firmware (the examples)

VS Code Pico extension (Compile / Run), or from a terminal with `PICO_SDK_PATH`
set:

    cmake -B build-rp2040 -G Ninja
    ninja -C build-rp2040

This builds two firmwares, each named with the chip (`RP2040` or `RP2350`) and also
copied to the top-level folder:

- `picocalc-remote-kbd-example-<chip>.uf2` from `examples/remote_test.c`
- `picocalc-remote-kbd-cursor-<chip>.uf2` from `demo/cursor_demo.c`

Flash by copying a `.uf2` to the `RPI-RP2` drive: hold BOOTSEL on power-up, or press
`~` (SHIFT + backtick) on the PicoCalc while one of these firmwares is running.

### Relay, Windows (MSYS2 UCRT64 shell, SDL2 installed)

    cmake -S desktop -B build-windows -G Ninja
    ninja -C build-windows

Output: `picocalc-remote-kbd-relay-Windows.exe` in the top-level folder. SDL2 is
linked statically, so it is one self-contained file. Add `-DRELAY_WITH_MIRROR=OFF`
to the first command for a relay without the demo's screen drawing.

### Relay, Linux (needs an SDL2 development package, e.g. `libsdl2-dev`)

    cmake -S desktop -B build-linux
    cmake --build build-linux

Output: `picocalc-remote-kbd-relay-Linux` plus `libSDL2-2.0.so.0` in the
top-level folder. SDL2 is linked dynamically; keep the two files side by side
(the executable finds the library through an `$ORIGIN` run-path).

## Running

1. Flash a `.uf2` to the PicoCalc and let it boot. A new serial port appears on the
   PC (Device Manager on Windows, or `ls /dev/ttyACM*` on Linux).
2. Start the relay. With no argument it finds the PicoCalc by its USB ID
   (`F00F:F00D`); you can also name the port yourself:

       picocalc-remote-kbd-relay-Windows.exe            (auto-detect)
       picocalc-remote-kbd-relay-Windows.exe COM5
       ./picocalc-remote-kbd-relay-Linux                (auto-detect)
       ./picocalc-remote-kbd-relay-Linux /dev/ttyACM0

3. Click the relay window to start capturing. Keys and mouse movement now go to the
   PicoCalc. Press **Ctrl+Alt+G** to release (the window also releases if it loses
   focus; any keys still held are sent a release so none get stuck).

The relay console can also log what goes through: press **Ctrl+Alt+L** (with the relay window focused) to turn it on or off; it starts off. While on it prints `[PC key]` for each key press and release the relay sends, `[PC mouse]` for mouse movement (added up once per loop) and buttons, and `[PicoCalc key]` for keys typed on the PicoCalc. The default is `RELAY_LOG_INPUT_DEFAULT` in `desktop/relay_config.h`. Text from `remote_log()` (`[PicoCalc] ...`) always prints. When it starts, the relay prints its version and a list of all its hotkeys.

The window border is the status colour: blue = idle, green = capturing, orange =
PicoCalc keys are typing into the PC, red = serial link lost. If the link is lost (USB cable pulled out, PicoCalc reset or re-flashed) the relay keeps running and looks for the PicoCalc again every second, reconnecting by itself when it reappears; you just click the window to capture again.

### Which firmware file do I flash?

Four firmware files are built, but you flash only **one**. Two choices:

**1. Which chip is in your PicoCalc?** `RP2040` or `RP2350`. Each chip needs its own
build, and the wrong one will not work. Hold BOOTSEL while powering on: the drive that
appears is called `RPI-RP2` for an RP2040, or `RP2350` for an RP2350.

**2. Which program?**

- **Cursor demo** (`picocalc-remote-kbd-cursor-<chip>.uf2`): the one most people want.
  An arrow that follows the mouse and a text area you can type into from either
  keyboard, with a live copy of the PicoCalc's screen in the relay window. The
  PicoCalc's own keys are also sent to the relay.
- **Example** (`picocalc-remote-kbd-example-<chip>.uf2`): the smallest possible program,
  with no display. It sends every key and mouse event it receives straight back, so the
  relay's console shows lines like `[PicoCalc] KEY usage=0x04 down`, plus a
  once-a-second `[PicoCalc] heartbeat` line. It shows the minimum code needed to use the
  library.

| | RP2040 | RP2350 |
|---|--------|--------|
| **Cursor demo** | `picocalc-remote-kbd-cursor-RP2040.uf2` | `picocalc-remote-kbd-cursor-RP2350.uf2` |
| **Example** | `picocalc-remote-kbd-example-RP2040.uf2` | `picocalc-remote-kbd-example-RP2350.uf2` |

## Typing the PicoCalc's keys into the PC (Windows)

Press **Ctrl+Alt+K** (from any window) to turn this on or off; it starts off.
While on, every key you press on the PicoCalc's own keyboard is typed into
whichever PC window has the focus, and the relay window's border turns orange.
It needs the optional `picocalc_keys` module in the firmware (both examples have
it). Capture (sending the PC's keyboard and mouse to the PicoCalc) and injection
never run together, because a key typed into the relay window would be sent
straight back to the PicoCalc and round again; turning injection on stops capture,
and capture will not start while it is on. Turning injection off releases any keys
still held. On Linux, Ctrl+Alt+K just reports that this is not supported yet;
everything else, including sending the PC's keyboard and mouse to the PicoCalc,
works the same on Linux and Windows.

## Status

Tested on hardware with RP2040 and RP2350 PicoCalcs and the Windows relay (2026-09-30), on the final V0.01A build (after the code review fixes):

| Feature | Status |
|---------|--------|
| PC keyboard, mouse movement and buttons to the PicoCalc | Working |
| PicoCalc text log back to the PC (`remote_log`) | Working |
| Relay finds the PicoCalc by USB ID | Working on Windows (SetupAPI) |
| Arrow cursor and typing demo on the LCD | Working |
| Live copy of the PicoCalc screen in the relay window | Working |
| PicoCalc's own keys sent to the relay | Working |
| PicoCalc's keys typed into the PC (Ctrl+Alt+K) | Working on Windows |
| RP2040 and RP2350 firmware | Both working: the cursor demo was flashed to an RP2040 and to an RP2350 PicoCalc and everything above works on each (the example firmware builds for both chips but was not separately run) |
| Relay reconnects by itself after a lost link (cable pulled out, PicoCalc reset or re-flashed) | Working (unplug and replug tested) |
| Linux relay | Written but not built or tested: port auto-detect (sysfs) and the serial code. Typing into the PC is a stub there ("not supported yet") |

Not done yet: clicking to place the text cursor and Delete/Home/End in the demo's
text area, non-US keyboard layouts, and mouse injection (the PicoCalc driving the
PC's pointer).
